events.title: First Fleet Arrives at Sydney Cove
events.description: Captain Arthur Phillip led the First Fleet of British ships carrying convicts, marines, and officials to Sydney Cove and raised the British flag, establishing the penal colony of New South Wales.
events.significance: The date marks the beginning of British colonization of Australia. It is observed as Australia Day, though many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people mark it as Invasion Day or Survival Day because of its impact on Indigenous peoples.

events.title: Michigan Admitted as the 26th U.S. State
events.description: Michigan was admitted to the Union as the 26th state after resolving the Toledo War border dispute with Ohio, receiving the Upper Peninsula as part of the settlement.
events.significance: Michigan's admission expanded the United States in the Great Lakes region and later made it a major center of industry, especially automobile manufacturing.

events.title: Constitution of India Comes into Effect
events.description: India's Constitution took effect, and India became a sovereign democratic republic. Rajendra Prasad was sworn in as its first President. The date was chosen to commemorate the 1930 Purna Swaraj declaration.
events.significance: The day is celebrated annually as Republic Day in India and marks the country's transition from a dominion to a republic with the world's longest written national constitution.

events.title: Louisiana Secedes from the Union
events.description: Louisiana voted to secede from the United States, becoming the sixth state to do so, and later joined the Confederate States of America.
events.significance: Its secession placed the vital port of New Orleans and the Mississippi River mouth under Confederate control, strengthening the Confederacy in the early days of the American Civil War.

events.title: Fall of Khartoum
events.description: Forces of the Mahdi captured Khartoum in Sudan after a long siege, killing British General Charles George Gordon and the defenders of the city.
events.significance: The fall of Khartoum was a major blow to British imperial prestige and prompted public outcry in Britain, contributing to the fall of Gladstone's government's popularity and reshaping British policy in Sudan.
